entries.title: Pakistan ends 'luxury tax' on menstrual products, contraceptives. Will prices drop?
entries.snippet: In Pakistan, taxes on menstrual products can add up. Activists have long worked to change this. Now a new budget wipes out the 18% sales tax. But questions remain about the impact on prices.

entries.title: Taiwan says Chinese pressure over the island is the 'new normal'

entries.snippet: Senators wanted to fast-track President Trump's pick for Director of National Intelligence. But Trump now says he wants to delay until they pass voting legislation that already failed in the Senate.

entries.snippet: People who go to prison keep one important right — to file a grievance over their treatment: from abuse to denied medical care. But in the vast majority of cases, those efforts go nowhere, according to an analysis of federal data by The Marshall Project and NPR.

entries.snippet: All detainees at an immigration detention center in an isolated airstrip in the Florida Everglades, known as "Alligator Alcatraz," have been transferred to other facilities, the U.S. Department of Homeland Security said, citing concerns related to the hurricane season.

entries.snippet: President Donald Trump is not known to be a fan of international gatherings of world leaders, but he changed his tune at this year's G7 summit at a French Alpine resort, where he was buoyed by support from his counterparts for his tentative agreement with Iran to end the war.

entries.snippet: On Wednesday night, the French president threw open Louis XIV's palace to his U.S. counterpart for a private reception, show and dinner marking America's 250th birthday.

entries.title: The private school choice boom leaves behind many kids in public school
entries.snippet: Soon, half of all American schoolkids will live in states that offer public money for a private education. Texas is the latest to join in, budgeting $1 billion to spend this fall on private school scholarships or homeschooling expenses.

entries.title: LIVE MAP: Track the path of Tropical Storm Arthur

entries.snippet: The Trump administration is giving Indiana more flexibility over how it decides to spend its federal grant money, the third state to receive such exemptions from the Education Department as it seeks to "return education to the states."

entries.title: The price tag of overcoming a Trump endorsement, and other takeaways from Tuesday's primaries

entries.title: Judge upholds the conviction of former Wisconsin judge Hannah Dugan for helping immigrant evade ICE
entries.snippet: A federal judge on Tuesday declined to overturn a Wisconsin judge's obstruction of justice conviction for helping a man evade immigration officers who showed up at a courtroom looking to detain him.

entries.title: Zelenskyy says G7 leaders pledge more vital help for Ukraine against Russia
entries.snippet: Leaders attending the Group of Seven summit in France promised to strengthen Ukraine's air defenses and ensure its energy supply, as well as step up international economic pressure on Moscow.

entries.snippet: The interim agreement ends fighting on all fronts for 60 days and sets out provisions for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

entries.title: EU lawmakers approve new tougher migrant policy
entries.snippet: The EU is backing tougher migration policies that seek to ramp up deportations of failed asylum-seekers. Under the new legislation, EU states can establish "return hubs."

entries.title: Germany: Reports of antisemitism in 2025 remain high
entries.snippet: The Federal Association of Departments for Research and Information on Antisemitism (RIAS) recorded over 8,700 cases they classify as antisemitic hostility in 2025, many of which were connected with the State of Israel.

entries.title: Middle East: Trump could restart Iran war if deal not signed
entries.snippet: President Trump says the US would "start the process again" if Iran doesn't make a deal. Meanwhile, Lebanon's president said talks with Israel are independent and should not be linked to the US-Iran deal. Follow DW.

entries.title: EU, G7 pledge support amid DRC Ebola outbreak
entries.snippet: G7 leaders called for a "strong and coordinated response" to the latest Ebola outbreak. The EU's Ursula von der Leyen said that "health security is shared security." The recorded death toll in DRC is approaching 200.

entries.title: CRISPR gene-editing for crops: Precision tool or new risk?
entries.snippet: The EU has eased restrictions on crops developed using novel genetic techniques. While supporters say the technology could help farmers adapt to climate change, critics argue its effects remain poorly understood.

entries.title: Morocco: The 2030 World Cup is more than sports, it is a national project
entries.snippet: Hosting the 2030 World Cup is more than just a sporting event for Rabat. While the kingdom invests heavily in infrastructure and prestige projects, doubts and social conflicts grow alongside a sense of pride and hope.

entries.title: Diplomats and abuse — chipping at the shield of immunity
entries.snippet: Domestic workers who were mistreated by diplomats are often denied justice due to their abusers enjoying diplomatic immunity. But court rulings in the UK and Switzerland have paved the way for change.

entries.title: World Cup 2026: Africa's new era takes shape
entries.snippet: From Cape Verde's debut to DR Congo's return, Africa's expanded presence at the 2026 World Cup brings new stories and renewed expectations of success.

entries.title: Iran's hardliners fear being sidelined in US deal
entries.snippet: As an Iran-US memorandum aimed at ending the war moves closer to formal signature, hardline supporters of the Islamic Republic fear losing influence as Iran's politics shift from maximalist defiance to compromise.

entries.title: NATO chief focuses on alliance unity after US alters pledges
entries.snippet: NATO's secretary general went to great lengths to cast a positive light on the alliance ahead of a ministers' meeting. The closest he came to addressing any tension was saying members have "a lot to talk about."

entries.title: Germany World Cup shirts run out of letter V
entries.snippet: Bad news for fans of Germany players Kai Havertz, Deniz Undav and Aleksandar Pavlovic: the kit makers have run out of the letter V, such is the demand for those names on shirts. But don't worry, more Vs are on the way!

entries.title: Ebola and the US patient spotlight global health 'injustice'
entries.snippet: The story of the US doctor who survived Ebola with experimental treatment in Germany highlights wider inequities in global health. It also reveals how sharply medical standards can differ between African countries.

entries.title: South Korea to shrink security buffer zone to North Korea
entries.snippet: South Korea will ease restrictions on roughly 270 square kilometers of land near the border with North Korea. Farmers in the area had long complained of rules that complicated working conditions.

entries.title: India: Telegram to challenge government order blocking app
entries.snippet: Telegram has reportedly challenged the Indian government's order to temporarily block the popular messaging app ahead of the NEET medical entrance exam.

entries.title: Germany news: Ministers discuss refugee deportation rules
entries.snippet: Germany's regional interior ministers are holding their biannual conference with immigration, deportations and benefits high on the agenda. Meanwhile, Germany and Poland are marking 35 years of cooperation. DW has more.

entries.title: Is Russia heading for a fuel crisis?
entries.snippet: Russia's fuel output is falling after Ukrainian drone strikes on refineries. Seasonal spikes in gasoline and diesel demand could push the system into a deeper crisis, experts say.

entries.title: Why the Williams sisters and other stars are playing longer
entries.snippet: More than three decades after they burst onto the tennis scene, Venus and Serena Williams are still playing at the top level. Why are we seeing elite athletes carrying on into their 40s and beyond?

entries.title: Bavarian top court rules state spy agency can monitor AfD
entries.snippet: Bavaria's regional domestic intelligence agency can monitor the right-wing populist AfD, the state's top court has ruled. Several states are trying to implement similar steps, with the opposition party challenging it.
